title: Cloud-scale Gas Properties, Depletion Times, and Star Formation Efficiency per Freefall Time in PHANGS─ALMA
question: How do the regional mass-weighted cloud-scale (60-150 pc) molecular gas properties (surface density, velocity dispersion, virial parameter, free-fall time) relate to molecular gas depletion time and star formation efficiency per free-fall time in 1.5 kpc regions across PHANGS-ALMA galaxies?

recipe.goal: Convert CO (2-1) intensity to molecular gas mass with a variable alpha_CO
recipe.method: Local best-estimate alpha_CO^2-1 = alpha_CO,MW^1-0 x f(Z) x g(Sigma_star) x R21(Sigma_SFR)^-1 applied region by region
key_parameters: Emissivity term alpha_CO^1-0 ~ Sigma_star^-0.25 for Sigma_star > 100 Msun pc^-2
assumptions: alpha_CO assumed fixed within each region when averaging

recipe.goal: Measure cloud-scale gas properties along each CO-detected line of sight at 150 pc
recipe.method: Per sightline: Sigma_mol, effective-width sigma_mol, R_pix, then tau_ff and alpha_vir; face-on and completeness corrections
key_parameters: tau_ff = sqrt(3 pi / (32 G rho)), rho = 3 M_beam / (4 pi R_pix^3)
R_pix = (l^2 H_mol / (8 cos i))^(1/3), l = 150 pc, H_mol = 100 pc
assumptions: Mass in each beam spread over the whole beam and a line-of-sight depth H_mol / cos i

recipe.goal: Average cloud-scale properties over 1.5 kpc hexagonal regions with mass weighting
recipe.method: Each sightline weighted by local gas surface density within each hexagon; tau_ff averaged harmonically so tau_dep ~ <tau_ff> for fixed eps_ff
key_parameters: Hexagonal apertures 1.5 kpc diameter (1 kpc for the 120/90/60 pc samples)

recipe.method: Convolve Sigma_SFR and Sigma_mol maps to 1.5 kpc FWHM, divide for tau_dep, sample at hexagon centre; eps_ff = <tau_ff> / tau_dep
key_parameters: Sigma_SFR from H-alpha + WISE 22 um (default); GALEX FUV + WISE 22 um where H-alpha missing; WISE 22 um alone in a handful of cases
assumptions: Sigma_SFR estimators match VLT/MUSE gold-standard maps to ~0.1 dex accuracy

recipe.goal: Select regions with adequate CO completeness
recipe.method: Require cloud-scale CO flux completeness > 50% and <Sigma_mol^cloud> > 20 Msun pc^-2
assumptions: Lognormal surface-density PDF used to correct for completeness (inherited from Sun et al. 2022)

recipe.goal: Correlate and fit tau_dep and eps_ff against cloud-scale gas properties
recipe.method: Spearman rank correlation plus a linear fit y = m (x - x0) + b in log-log space, treating the gas property as the independent variable; also galaxy-normalised versions and KDE median trends
key_parameters: x0 is the median of x; intrinsic scatter term included but very small; sigma reported as robust rms residual
Adopted uncertainties: tau_dep 0.3 dex, Sigma_mol 0.2 dex, tau_ff 0.1 dex, sigma_mol 0.15 dex
assumptions: Fit y on x (not x on y, not bivariate); results depend on this choice

recipe.goal: Test robustness to alpha_CO and resolution
recipe.method: Repeat the analysis with a fixed Galactic alpha_CO and with 120, 90 and 60 pc cloud-scale data in 1 kpc hexagons

score_reason: The paper gives a step-by-step appendix, explicit formulae and numeric fit tables, but depends on mega-tables and inputs from earlier papers and omits bootstrap and fit settings.
rediscovery_reason: Region tables are online and the appendix gives a complete recipe; headline slopes and eps_ff are numeric, so a reproduction from the mega-tables is feasible.
